answer: Nectar-route attestation. Each identity must publish a signed route through a fixed set of relay nodes; relays only forward work whose route token carries a fresh nectar marker derived from their own secret. Duplicating an identity forces the attacker to acquire distinct relay markers, and each marker requires a live handshake with an independent relay that logs the pairing. A violet flag marks any token reuse across routes, revealing clones. The orchard of relays therefore grows the attacker's cost linearly: every extra identity needs its own relay handshakes,
